empty.no_dataset.hint: Import a CSV event log or load the synthetic purchase-to-pay demo to get started.
empty.no_match.title: No cases match the current filters
empty.no_match.hint: Remove a filter chip to widen the selection.
empty.no_match.hint_total: The dataset has {total} cases. Remove a filter chip to widen the selection.
filters.title: Case filters
filters.intro: Filters select cases; every selected case keeps its complete event history. All criteria combine with AND. The same filters apply to KPIs, graphs, variants, cases, comparisons and exports.
filters.hint: Variant and transition filters are set from the Variants and Process pages and shown as chips. Hold Ctrl/⌘ to select several values in a list.
filters.none: No filters — all cases of the dataset are included.
graph.tip.click_node: Click to list cases with this activity
ov.intro: Key figures for the cases selected by the current filters. Each figure states the population it is computed on.
ov.kpi.cases_title: Distinct case IDs in the selection
ov.kpi.events_title: Retained events of the selected cases
ov.no_completed: No completed cases in the selection (check the completion rule on the Datasets page).
ov.interpolation_note: median and p90 use linear interpolation
ov.dur.observed_note: last − first event timestamp; includes cases that may still be running
ov.dur.throughput_note: cases completed per the dataset's completion rule
ov.dur.throughput_note_none: no completion rule configured: no case is known to be completed
ov.bottlenecks_note: Transitions with the longest median elapsed time (≥ 5 cases). Elapsed time between events can include waiting and work; it is a starting point for investigation, not a root cause.
ov.no_bottlenecks: No transitions observed in at least 5 cases.
proc.intro: A directly-follows graph of the selected cases: an edge A → B means B was the next recorded event after A in the same case. It is not a BPMN model and does not show causality, concurrency or decision logic.
proc.animate_flow_title: Moving dashes show the direction of each transition
proc.animate_flow_disabled: Animations are turned off in Settings
proc.legend.width: Edge width ∝ occurrences (frequency) or elapsed time (time mode)
proc.legend.slow: Time mode: elapsed time above half of the maximum
proc.legend.counts: Edge occurrences = total times the transition happened; distinct cases = cases containing it at least once (hover an edge).
proc.legend.elapsed: Elapsed time = difference between consecutive event timestamps (d = days, h = hours). It can include waiting and work.
proc.legend.thresholds: Thresholds only hide elements in this drawing; KPIs and other pages are unaffected.
proc.legend.click: Click an activity or edge to list the matching cases.
proc.stats: {cases} cases (of {total}) · {events} events · {nodes} activities · {edges} edges incl. start/end
proc.visibility: Showing {shownNodes} of {totalNodes} activities and {shownEdges} of {totalEdges} edges (including start/end edges). Hidden elements remain part of every calculation.
var.intro: A variant is the ordered sequence of activities of a case. Select a variant to highlight its path and list its cases. Durations are observed (last − first event) and include cases that may still be running.
var.graph_label: Process graph with the selected variant highlighted
var.select_cases_hint: Select a variant to list its cases.
var.summary: {variants} variants across {cases} cases. Repeated activities are highlighted. Shares are of the filtered cases.
cs.intro: Every case selected by the filters, with its complete event history. Click a case to open its timeline.
cs.select_hint: Select a case to see its timeline.
cs.summary: {n} of {total} cases match. Times shown in {tz}.
cs.ties_note: Some events share a timestamp (orange markers). Their order follows the source row and does not establish which happened first.
cs.no_rules: No conformance rules defined for this dataset.
cs.tie_title: Shares its timestamp with a neighbouring event
perf.intro: Elapsed times between consecutive events, and comparisons by resource, department and user-defined cohorts. These are descriptive associations within the selected cases, not proof of root causes.
perf.elapsed_note: Elapsed time = timestamp of an event minus the timestamp of the preceding event in the same case. It can contain waiting and processing.
perf.execution_note: Execution duration = completion − start timestamp, only for events that have both.
perf.cohorts_note: Both cohorts are subsets of the cases selected by the global filters above. Leave a field empty to not constrain it.
perf.not_mapped: No values for “{field}” are mapped in this dataset.
perf.small_cohort: At least one cohort has fewer than 30 cases; medians and p90 values are unstable.
perf.activity_share: Share of cases containing each activity
cf.intro_1: Rule-based conformance: each case is checked against configurable business rules. Results:
cf.intro_2: the last one when the data cannot establish compliance (for example, the case is not known to be complete, or events share a timestamp). Formal Petri-net replay or alignments are not part of this version.
cf.delete_confirm: Delete rule “{name}”? Alert rules based on it and their alerts are deleted too.
cf.none.title: No rules yet
cf.none.hint: Create a rule to check cases against your business requirements.
rule.help.required_activity: Compliant if the activity occurs. Absent in a complete case → violating; absent in an open case → not evaluable.
rule.help.forbidden_activity: Violating if the activity occurs at least once. Absent in an open case → not evaluable.
rule.help.precedence: Every occurrence of B needs an A with a strictly earlier timestamp. A tie with A → not evaluable. No B in a complete case → compliant (vacuous).
rule.help.max_duration: Completed throughput: only completed cases are judged. Observed duration: every case as recorded so far.
rule.help.max_occurrences: Violating when the activity occurs more often than allowed (repeats count). Open cases under the limit → not evaluable.
rule.help.start_activity: The first event must be one of the activities. Several events tied at the first timestamp with mixed activities → not evaluable.
rule.help.end_activity: Only complete cases are judged; the last event must be one of the activities.
rule.desc.max_throughput: completed throughput must be at most {hours} h
rule.desc.max_observed: observed duration must be at most {hours} h
conf.dur.not_completed: Throughput is defined only for completed cases (this case: {status}).
conf.dur.within: {hours} h is within the {limit} h limit.
conf.dur.over_open: {hours} h exceeds the {limit} h limit (observed so far; the case is not known to be complete).
conf.dur.within_open: {hours} h is within the {limit} h limit (observed so far; the case is not known to be complete).
conf.req.absent_open: '{activity}' has not occurred yet and the case is not known to be complete.
conf.forb.absent_open: '{activity}' has not occurred so far, but the case is not known to be complete.
conf.maxocc.open: '{activity}' occurs {count} time(s) so far and the case is not known to be complete.
conf.prec.a_done: '{a}' already occurred and '{b}' has not occurred yet.
conf.prec.none_yet: Neither '{a}' nor '{b}' occurred yet and the case is not known to be complete.
conf.prec.tie: {count} occurrence(s) of '{b}' share a timestamp with '{a}'; order cannot be established.
conf.start.tie_ok: All {count} events at the first timestamp are allowed ({activities}).
conf.start.tie_bad: The first event(s) {activities} are not allowed.
conf.start.tie_mixed: {count} events share the first timestamp ({activities}); their order cannot be established.
conf.end.tie_ok: All {count} events at the last timestamp are allowed ({activities}).
conf.end.tie_bad: The last event(s) {activities} are not allowed.
conf.end.tie_mixed: {count} events share the last timestamp ({activities}); their order cannot be established.
conf.end.open: The end activity cannot be judged because the case is not known to be complete.
al.intro: In-app alerts created by alert rules. One alert per rule and case: re-evaluating updates existing alerts instead of duplicating them, and never resets the status you set.
al.no_monitoring_detail: Rules are evaluated only when you click “Evaluate rules now” and automatically after each successful import. No e-mails, messages or external system actions are sent.
al.need_conformance_rule: Create a conformance rule first (Conformance page).
al.rule_created: Alert rule created — click “Evaluate rules now” to generate alerts.
al.delete_confirm: Delete alert rule “{name}” and its alerts?
al.none_hint: Evaluate the alert rules to check for new alerts.
al.condition_gone: Condition no longer met at the last evaluation.
al.counts: This dataset: {open} open · {acknowledged} acknowledged · {resolved} resolved alerts.
al.no_rules.title: No alert rules
al.no_rules.hint: Create one to start tracking cases.
al.eval_detail: Rules evaluated: {rules}. New alerts: {created}, updated: {updated}, no longer matching: {gone}.
alert.metric.open_case_age: Open-case age at reference time (incomplete/unknown cases)
alert.msg.open_age: Open-case age {hours} h at reference time {reference} exceeds {limit} h.
ds.intro: Imported event logs persist in the local database. Each re-import creates a new dataset version.
ds.demo_loaded_detail: {cases} synthetic cases, {events} events. Example rules were added and {alerts} alerts were created by the post-import evaluation.
ds.delete.title: Delete dataset
ds.delete.warning: This permanently removes the dataset, its events, import findings, conformance rules, alert rules and alerts. This cannot be undone.
ds.delete.type_name: Type the dataset name to confirm:
ds.report.title: Import findings — {name} (v{version})
ds.report.summary: {rows} source rows → {events} events imported, {quarantined} rows quarantined.
ds.settings.title: Analysis settings — {name}
ds.settings.name: Name
ds.settings.reference_time: Reference time for open-case age (UTC; empty = latest event)
ds.settings.completion_note: A case is never treated as complete just because no later event was observed. Choose an explicit completion rule.
ds.settings.saved: Settings saved. Analyses now use the new settings.
ds.none.title: No datasets yet
ds.none.hint: Load the synthetic demo data or import your own CSV event log.
completion.end_activity: Completed when the last event is an end activity
imp.title: Import an event log
imp.intro: Upload a CSV, map its columns to the event schema, choose how timestamps are read, review every validation finding and then confirm. Nothing is imported until you confirm.
imp.upload.title: Upload a CSV file
imp.upload.drop: Drop a CSV file here or choose one.
imp.upload.required: Required columns: case ID, activity, timestamp. Identifiers are read as text, so leading zeros are kept.
imp.upload.no_file: No file at hand? Download a sample:
imp.reread_done: File re-read with the selected encoding and delimiter.
imp.no_data_rows: The file has no data rows.
imp.ts.intro: Timestamps with an explicit offset (e.g. Z or +02:00) use that offset. All others are interpreted in the source timezone and converted to UTC.
imp.ts.suggestion_note: The suggested format is the candidate that parses the largest share of the first 500 sampled values. Day/month order cannot be inferred reliably — check it.
imp.ts.map_first: Map the timestamp column to get format suggestions.
imp.ts.shift_forward: Shift forward to a valid time
imp.ts.shift_backward: Shift backward to a valid time
imp.v.invalid_hint: Fix the file or the options, or choose the quarantine policy in the next step. Invalid rows are never dropped silently.
imp.v.ties_hint: They are ordered by source row, which does not establish a reliable causal order.
imp.v.rework_kept: Repeated activities are kept: they can represent legitimate rework.
imp.v.truncated: Showing the first findings; download the report for all.
imp.policy.reject: Reject the import if any row is invalid
imp.policy.quarantine: Import valid rows and quarantine invalid rows (kept aside with reasons, excluded from analysis)
imp.completion_note: The last observed event is not proof that a case is finished. Without a rule, all cases are “unknown” and throughput metrics stay empty.
imp.reference_time: Reference time for open-case age (UTC, optional)
job.error.interrupted: The server stopped while this import was running. No data from it was committed. Start the import again from the import wizard.
import.rejected_invalid: Import rejected: {invalid} of {total} rows are invalid. Fix the file, adjust the mapping/timestamp options, or choose the quarantine policy.
import.no_valid_rows: No valid rows remain after validation; nothing was imported.
import.target_deleted: The target dataset was deleted while the import was running.
import.alerts_failed: Alert evaluation failed after import; run it again from the Alerts page.
import.internal_error: The import failed due to an internal error. No data was committed; see the server log.

finding.nonexistent_local_time: Local time does not exist in {timezone} (DST change). Choose a nonexistent-time policy ('shift_forward' or 'shift_backward') to import it.

finding.nonexistent_time_resolved: {count} nonexistent local timestamp(s) shifted using policy '{policy}'.

finding.negative_cost: {count} row(s) have a negative cost (kept as-is).

finding.whitespace_trimmed: Leading/trailing whitespace was trimmed from {count} value(s).

note.dfg.edge: Directly-follows graph: an edge A→B means B was the next recorded event after A in the same case.
note.dfg.not_bpmn: It is not a BPMN model and does not show causality, concurrency or decision logic.
note.dfg.elapsed: Elapsed time is the difference between consecutive event timestamps; it can include waiting and processing and is not labeled as either.
note.perf.transitions: Transition times are elapsed times between consecutive events (they may include waiting and work).
note.perf.participation: Resource/department 'elapsed before event' is the time from the preceding event in the same case to an event performed by that resource/department.
note.perf.descriptive: Comparisons are descriptive associations within the selected population, not proof of root causes.
note.cmp.population: Both cohorts are drawn from the population selected by the global filters.
note.cmp.descriptive: Differences are descriptive associations and do not establish causes.
note.cmp.small: Small cohorts produce unstable medians and p90 values; check the case counts.
note.conf.rule_based: Rule-based conformance: each case is checked against this business rule only. This is not Petri-net replay or alignment-based conformance.
note.conf.not_evaluable: 'not evaluable' means the data cannot establish compliance yet (e.g. the case is not known to be complete, or events share a timestamp so their order is unknown).
demo.description: SYNTHETIC demo data: an invented purchase-to-pay process (600 cases). Not real business data.
set.intro: Preferences of the local user. They are stored in the ProcessLens database and apply to every page.
set.language_note: Interface texts, explanations, validation messages and alerts are shown in this language. Your data (activity names, case IDs) is never translated.
set.animations_note: Page transitions, counters, chart and graph animations, and the flow animation in the process explorer.
set.motion.system_hint: Animate unless the operating system asks for reduced motion.
set.os_reduced: Your operating system currently requests reduced motion.
set.os_normal: Your operating system does not request reduced motion.
